sentences.text: All species of Caseodus grew to approximately 1 to 1.5 meters in length.
The Triassic species completely lacked upper jaws and featured an elongated projection called a rostrum extending from the lower jaw to support the tooth-whorl.
The genus Caseodus was described by Zangerl in 1981.
The genus name honors paleoichthyologist Gerard Case, and the type species was originally classified in the genus Orodus.
Caseodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Eugeneodontiformes that lived during the Carboniferous period.
It is classified within the family Caseodontidae.
Caseodus lived during the Carboniferous period in what is now the Midwestern United States and potentially the Early Triassic in what is now British Columbia, Canada.
It is debated whether the Early Triassic species C. varidentis belongs in the genus Caseodus due to its significantly different skull and tooth morphology.
